slides.explanation: The attack on the central Ukrainian city resulted in two deaths and dozens of injuries. This follows a pattern of strikes on civilian areas.

slides.headline: Ukraine doubles down on NATO membership
slides.explanation: Hours after the attack, President Zelensky reaffirmed that Ukraine still intends to join NATO.
Five major international outlets including the BBC and Al Jazeera confirmed these details. When diverse global newsrooms report the same facts, it indicates a high level of verification.

caption:
A Russian ballistic missile struck President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine this Saturday.

The attack resulted in two confirmed deaths and left dozens of others wounded.

Following the strike, President Zelensky reiterated his government's firm commitment to joining NATO. Ukraine is currently exploring security guarantees that would mirror the support provided by the military alliance.

We have verified these reports across five independent international news organizations. This ensures you are getting the facts without the noise.

story.title: Russia attacks Zelensky's hometown, Ukraine reaffirms wish to join NATO
story.summary: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.
